claims.rationale: The frontmatter registers a PreToolUse hook on the Bash and PowerShell tools that runs a checking script before each command (lines 1-24). The body says that when a destructive command is detected the person is warned 'and can choose to proceed or cancel' (line 32): a command matching a listed pattern (recursive delete, DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, force-push, git reset --hard, kubectl delete and similar; lines 40-50) returns a permission decision of ask (line 81), while two catastrophic shapes are denied outright (lines 86-89). The decision on a destructive command therefore moves from the model to the person, and the mechanism is the harness hook rather than the model's compliance. Limits the text states: on PowerShell, string matching 'can't see a command built at' runtime (line 67); compound commands fall through to the ask tier (lines 90-91); it is 'A best-effort advisory hard-stop, not a policy boundary' (line 91); deletions of common build directories are allowed without warning (lines 72-75); the hooks are session-scoped (line 103). Plausible failure modes: in an unattended session the ask has no responder and the run parks; in a harness that does not execute skill-declared hooks the text has no effect at all. Falsified if a listed pattern executes without a prompt in a session meeting the conditions.
